say: You give it a segment $[AB]$. It draws the line that cuts $[AB]$ in half and meets it at a **right angle**.
The key idea: a point the same distance from $A$ and from $B$ lies on this line. Two such points are enough to draw it.

how.higher: It turned up in 2016, 2022 and 2024 on Paper 2, never as the main skill: it was a step inside a longer construction (the midpoint of a side, or the circumcentre).
how.ordinary: It was a part of its own in 2021 (5 marks, Paper 2, the bisector of a side of a triangle) and a step in 2025 (finding a midpoint).

example.question: Draw a segment $[AB]$ with $|AB| = 8$ cm. Using only a compass and straight edge, construct the perpendicular bisector of $[AB]$.

steps.title: Set the compass
steps.say: Open the compass to more than half of $|AB|$, about $5$ cm. Put the point on $A$ and draw an arc above and below the segment.

lines.text: Do not change the setting until both arcs are drawn.

steps.title: Repeat from the other end
steps.say: Keep the same setting. Put the point on $B$ and draw an arc above and below the segment, crossing the first two arcs.

lines.text: The arcs cross at two points, one above $[AB]$ and one below.

steps.title: Join the crossings
steps.say: With the ruler, draw a straight line through the two crossing points. Mark where it cuts $[AB]$ and call that point $M$.

lines.text: Leave every arc on the page. They are your construction lines and the marks are tied to them.
$|AM| = |MB| = 4$ cm and the line meets $[AB]$ at $90^\circ$.

Finding the midpoint is a mark of its own. Do it first and show it.
Label the point you are asked for. Leaving it unlabelled costs a mark even when the construction is right.

ordinary.tip: Draw the bisector of the side the question names. The wrong side loses a mark.

sources.quote: Draws perpendicular bisector of the side

ordinary.tip: Show the arcs. A midpoint or a perpendicular drawn without visible construction only earns partial credit.
The perpendicular must pass through the midpoint of the segment.

say: You give it the three side lengths of a triangle. It draws the triangle, accurately, with the arcs left showing.
The key idea: draw one side, then find the third vertex as the point where two arcs cross, one from each end of that side.

how.higher: It appeared once, in 2025 on Paper 2: a 5-mark part asking for a net, where one triangle was constructed from its three sides with the construction lines visible.
how.ordinary: It was the main skill in 2017 on Paper 2: a 10-mark part, constructing a triangle from three given lengths.

example.question: Construct the triangle $ABC$ with $|BC| = 7$ cm, $|AB| = 6$ cm and $|AC| = 4$ cm.

steps.title: Make a pilot sketch
steps.say: Sketch a rough triangle first and write the three lengths on it. This is the plan for the construction.

lines.text: A labelled pilot diagram earns marks even if the construction goes wrong.

steps.title: Draw the base
steps.say: With the ruler, draw $[BC]$ with $|BC| = 7$ cm. Label $B$ and $C$.

lines.text: Measure from the $0$ mark, not from the end of the ruler.

steps.title: Arc from B
steps.say: Set the compass to $6$ cm. Put the point on $B$ and draw an arc above $[BC]$.

lines.text: This arc holds every point that is $6$ cm from $B$.

steps.title: Arc from C
steps.say: Set the compass to $4$ cm. Put the point on $C$ and draw an arc that crosses the first one. Label the crossing $A$.

lines.text: $A$ is $6$ cm from $B$ and $4$ cm from $C$.

steps.title: Join up
steps.say: Join $A$ to $B$ and $A$ to $C$ with the ruler. Leave both arcs on the page.

lines.text: Check $|AB| = 6$ cm and $|AC| = 4$ cm with the ruler.

ordinary.tip: Draw a labelled pilot sketch first. It earns marks on its own.
Each correct length drawn earns marks, so get one side right before moving on.
Label the vertices. A correct construction with them named or omitted is not full marks.

say: You give it two sides of a triangle and the angle **between** them. It draws the triangle.
The key idea: the angle fixes the direction of the second side, and its length fixes where it stops. The third side is then just the line that joins the ends.
what.in: two sides and the angle between them

how.ordinary: It was the main skill in 2016 on Paper 2: part of a 5-mark question where the student drew a triangle from two sides and the angle between them, then measured the rest.

example.question: Construct the triangle $ABC$ with $|AB| = 6$ cm, $|BC| = 8$ cm and $|\angle ABC| = 70^\circ$.

steps.title: Make a pilot sketch
steps.say: Sketch a rough triangle and write $6$ cm, $8$ cm and $70^\circ$ on it, with the angle at $B$.

lines.text: The angle sits between the two given sides, so it goes at $B$.

steps.title: Draw the base
steps.say: With the ruler, draw $[BC]$ with $|BC| = 8$ cm. Label $B$ and $C$.

lines.text: Measure from the $0$ mark on the ruler.

steps.title: Measure the angle
steps.say: Put the protractor centre on $B$ with its base line along $[BC]$. Mark a dot at $70^\circ$. Draw a ray from $B$ through the dot.

lines.text: Read the scale that starts at $0^\circ$ on $[BC]$.

steps.title: Mark off the length
steps.say: On the ray, measure $6$ cm from $B$. Mark the point $A$.

lines.text: Make an arc or a clear mark so the $6$ cm can be seen.

steps.title: Join up
steps.say: Join $A$ to $C$ with the ruler. Label all three vertices.

lines.text: Leave the angle mark and the arc on the page.

Each correct element drawn (a line, an angle) earns marks, so draw them carefully one at a time.

sources.quote: One correct line or angle drawn.

say: You give it one side of a triangle and the two angles at its ends. It draws the triangle.
The key idea: each angle gives a ray from one end of the side. The third vertex is where the two rays meet.
what.in: one side and the two angles at its ends

how.ordinary: It was the main skill in 2018 on Paper 2: a 10-mark part, constructing a triangle from a side and two angles, then reading off the length of another side.

example.question: Construct the triangle $ABC$ with $|BC| = 8$ cm, $|\angle B| = 40^\circ$ and $|\angle C| = 65^\circ$.

steps.title: Make a pilot sketch
steps.say: Sketch a rough triangle. Write $8$ cm on $[BC]$, $40^\circ$ at $B$ and $65^\circ$ at $C$.

lines.text: Label the vertices now so you do not lose marks later.

steps.title: Draw the base
steps.say: With the ruler, draw $[BC]$ with $|BC| = 8$ cm. Label $B$ and $C$.

lines.text: The side is between the two angles, so both angles sit on it.

steps.title: Angle at B
steps.say: Put the protractor centre on $B$ with its base line along $[BC]$. Mark $40^\circ$ and draw a ray from $B$ through the mark.

lines.text: Read the scale that starts at $0^\circ$ on $[BC]$.

steps.title: Angle at C
steps.say: Put the protractor centre on $C$ with its base line along $[CB]$. Mark $65^\circ$ and draw a ray from $C$ through the mark.

lines.text: Now the base line points the other way, so start again from $0^\circ$ on $[CB]$.

steps.title: Find the vertex
steps.say: The two rays cross at one point. Label it $A$.

lines.text: Leave the angle marks on the page.
